burhczydx_10a.m: Who art thou that disturbeth the peace of an Elythom knight?
r: Oh, sorry. I'm already gone again.
I am looking for my brother Andor. Do you have seen him? He looks a bit like me.

burhczydx_10a_2.m: No, $playername. I have not seen Andor lately.
r: How do you know my name?

burhczydx_10a_3.m: Oops. Eh, well, we Elythom knights know many things.
r: That's not the whole truth. Now?

burhczydx_10a_4.m: All right, $playername. Of course I know you well. I am Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye.
r: Burhczyd? You - a Knight of Elythom?

burhczydx_10a_5.m: One should have that impression. But not everything is as it seems.

burhczydx_10a_6.m: You know, once I feasted with the Lord Commander of the Order of Elythom. A very pleasant man.

burhczydx_10a_6a.m: We got merry, and in high spirits I 'borrowed' a few little things from him.

burhczydx_10a_7.m: Now the whole order is looking for the thief. So I thought it wise to disguise myself.

burhczydx_10a_7a.m: Indeed. They'd never suspect this. I already talked with some knights and asked about their progress.

burhczydx_10a_7b.m: It was really hard to hold back my laughter.

burhczydx_10a_8.m: But now you should leave. Otherwise we may arouse suspicion.
r: You are right. We'll surely meet another time.

burhczydx_10e.m: We'd better not be seen together anymore.

r: Burhczyd - she really wants to marry you, doesn't she?
Now tell me - what exactly did she say?
Nothing?! And what did you all talk about?

burhczydx_11a_14.m: I haven't even spoken to her yet. I feared that she might laugh at me.
r: But you want her to marry you next month. How does that work?

burhczydx_11a_15.m: That might actually be difficult, yes.
r: You will go and talk to her. Repeat!

burhczydx_11a_16.m: I will go and talk to her.

burhczydx_11a_19.m: If you say so. Wish me luck!

r: When we last met you were dressed like a knight of the Elythom.
[mumbling] ... end in disaster again. Oh dear.
I'm very curious about the story now. Tell me how have you been since we last met? What about the Elythom?

burhczydx_11a_4.m: Oh that. I got bored playing Knight of the Elythom. I then spread the word that I was walking around dressed as one.

burhczydx_11a_5.m: They are still searching and now suspect each other! Extremely amusing!

burhczydx_11a_6.m: And now I will lead a serious and decent life. I owe that to my bride-to-be.

burhczydx_11a_7.m: Oh yes! She is the prettiest girl in the whole world!
r: I'm delighted for you! When will the wedding take place?

burhczydx_11a_9.m: Well, her parents haven't given me their consent yet.
r: Hmm, that might be difficult. But the main thing is that she wants you. Then it will be okay with the parents.

burhczydx_11e.m: I'm preparing a little love poem for my girl. As soon as I have the words I will go.

r: Hey, Burhczyd, nice to meet you again. What's new?

burhczydx_12a_10.m: But I'll show them. I've already bought my own oven. It will be installed next week.

r: [Muttering to yourself] Two things are infinite: the sky and Burhczyd's stupidity, but I'm not entirely sure about the sky.

burhczydx_12a_3.m: No. About mugs. They’re always empty when you need them most.

burhczydx_12a_5.m: Who am I talking about? WHO AM I TALKING ABOUT??
r: Eh ... Oh. Your love. I see.

burhczydx_12a_6.m: Of all the options she has, she chooses a baker. Why? Why?
r: Hmm, a baker can bake bridecake.

burhczydx_12a_7.m: I could have shown her the world...

r: Instead, fresh bread rolls every day.

burhczydx_12e.m: Look, my mug is still empty. Sigh.

r: Why is that oven here on the table?

burhczydx_13a_10.m: Not yet. But love is a fierce fire.

r: And if she still chooses him?

burhczydx_13a_13.m: Then I shall undercut his prices.

burhczydx_13a_14.m: [He nods, convinced.] Romance is much like trade. Except with more ovens.
r: I wish you luck. Much luck. You will need it.
Don't pretend. The oven is right in front of your nose.

burhczydx_13a_3.m: Ah that. [patting the oven fondly] Destiny is heavy, and the table here is strong, that's why.

burhczydx_13a_4.m: She is to marry a baker.

burhczydx_13a_5.m: Thus I, too, have become a baker. So easy.
r: You own no house. How will you do it?

burhczydx_13a_6.m: That is a detail. My bread will be larger. The largest ones far and wide.

burhczydx_13a_7.m: I shall bake such big loaves that she must notice me.
r: OK ... Where will you bake them?

burhczydx_13a_8.m: Here. Or there. Wherever the oven rests.

r: Do you know how to bake?

burhczydx_13e.m: The oven is still heating up; baking will take a while longer.

burhczydx_14a_10.m: Well, I have learned much in my still short holy life.

burhczydx_14a_11.m: That fasting is easier when one has never eaten well.

burhczydx_14a_12.m: Fasting, yes. [Rummaging in his sack] Fasting helps one progress on the path of knowledge. [Taking bread and cheese out of the sack]
r: Bread and cheese? Is that not against your vows?

burhczydx_14a_17.m: The abbot said I lacked discipline.

burhczydx_14a_18.m: An imaginary one. But he was very convincing.

burhczydx_14a_19.m: [Low voice] The holy life is not for everyone.

burhczydx_14a_2.m: $playername, don't you want to add something meaningful?
r: Burhczyd, is that really you? Last time I saw you running around with an oven.

burhczydx_14a_20.m: I miss ambition. And chairs with backs. But I don't miss ovens.

burhczydx_14a_3.m: Sigh. That was a long time ago. In a past life.

r: A good decision, I think. Was it profitable?

burhczydx_14a_5.m: Spiritually. [He folds his hands.] I have cast aside worldly burdens.

burhczydx_14a_6.m: I now live as a monk. I rise at dawn, pray at noon, and reflect at night.

burhczydx_14a_7.m: The silence here is very instructive. [He leans closer.] I have sworn a vow of poverty.

burhczydx_14a_8.m: This time it is intentional. [He sighs peacefully.]

burhczydx_14a_9.m: At last, I am free of desire. Eh, mostly.
r: Yes, I just saw that pretty girl too ...

burhczydx_14a_r5.m: Post ferrum, lac. Post lac, error.

burhczydx_14a_r6.m: Umbra fidelis non est post vesperum.

burhczydx_14a_r8.m: Denarius cadit sicut vult, non sicut debeo.

burhczydx_14a_r9.m: Septem gradus egi, octo recordor. Praemonitus eram, sed male.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_15e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_16e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_17e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_18e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_19e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

burhczydx_1a.m: Hi, who are you? I have never seen you here.
r: My name is $playername. I am from Crossglen.
My father always told me not to talk to strangers.

burhczydx_1a_2.m: Cool. I am Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye. Nice to meet you.
r: Burh... - eh, OK. Do you live here in this town?

burhczydx_1a_3.m: Yes. At least until now. My parents gave me some money so that I could tour the world. This morning I set off, and I'm staying here in the inn. However, I will have to earn some more money, otherwise it will be a short trip.
r: Yes, some gold always helps. Hmm, maybe you can kill two birds with one stone.
Take a cart and start a transport company. You can deliver goods to different cities and get some money.

burhczydx_1a_5.m: Wow, splendid idea! I will take my father's cart. Then all I need is a name for my company. Thanks for this tip.

burhczydx_1e.m: I am still thinking about what to call my company. As soon as I have a name, I'll start.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_20e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_21e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

r: Burhczyd, is it really you? Wait, don't run away ...

burhczydx_22e.m: As soon as ...todo..., I will go.

burhczydx_2a.m: Hi, we know each other! Unfortunately I forgot your name. Come, have a drink with me. How are you?
r: My name is $playername. And you are called something with Brr, as far as I can remember.

burhczydx_2a_2.m: Yes, almost: My name is Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye. I opened a transport company, as you suggested.
r: Great to hear! Is it going well? Do you already have many customers?

burhczydx_2a_3.m: Well, there are not too many yet.

burhczydx_2a_5.m: I have no idea. My beautiful cart with BURHCZYD AFGZ DTALOUMIYE - TRANSPORTS written in big white letters always runs empty.
r: Good grief! What did you name your company?!

burhczydx_2a_6.m: 'Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye - Transports'. Is there a problem with that?
r: Nobody can pronounce that name, let alone remember it. No wonder you do not get any orders!
Sure. You have to use a short and catchy name.

burhczydx_2a_8.m: OK, I'll think about a better company name.

burhczydx_2e.m: I am still thinking about a better name for my company. As soon as I have it, I'll leave.

burhczydx_3a.m: Hello ... eh, sorry, I forgot your name. How are you?

burhczydx_3a_2.m: Don't ask. Still no orders. And I have no idea why.
r: That's horrible! What did you call your company? It should be short and memorable.

burhczydx_3a_3.m: Yes, that's what I've done. You said 'Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye' was be too long and hard to remember, so I simply chose the initials of my name. Clever, right?

burhczydx_3a_4.m: It is now: 'B.A.D. TRANSPORTS' - it looks great!
r: You can't be serious!  BAD TRANSPORTS? Tell me that's just a joke!

burhczydx_3a_5.m: Oh no! Did I get it wrong again? Nothing I do ever works. (sob)
r: Look, just call your company 'Easy Transports'. That will do.

burhczydx_3a_6.m: OK, thank you. I'll try. Later. Tomorrow. Maybe. (sob)

burhczydx_3e.m: Only one more beer, then I'll leave.

r: I am fine. And my name is $playername, as you should know by now.
No, no! It is not for me. Unload the fish in the nearest forest and make a burnt offering.

burhczydx_4a_11.m: That is a great idea! The better the offering, the greater the help will be.
r: I hope it doesn't work the other way around

burhczydx_4a_12.m: Let's have a drink on this splendid idea!

burhczydx_4a_2.m: I am Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye, proud owner of Easy Transports.
r: The last time we saw each other, you did not have any transport orders yet.

burhczydx_4a_3.m: Oh, that has completely changed. I am into big business now.

burhczydx_4a_4.m: I just got a cartload of fresh fish in Remgard. I think I will sell it here with a high profit.

burhczydx_4a_5.m: In the last two cities, they could not afford to buy this quality fish. But it will work here. Certainly.

burhczydx_4a_6.m: Of course from Remgard, their fish is the best - a rare delicacy in this area!

r: Nothing. Because we have known each other for so long, I will suggest something.

burhczydx_4a_8.m: Fire away. Your ideas are always good.
r: I will buy your fish for, say, {1000} gold pieces.
I will buy your fish for, say, 100 gold pieces.
I will buy your fish for, say, 10 gold pieces.
I will take your fish, but I can't give you any money.

burhczydx_4e.m: Let's have another drink on this splendid idea, before I leave to do the offering.

burhczydx_5a_2.m: Is it? Anyway. Nice to meet you here. I want to thank you for your good advice.

burhczydx_5a_3.m: Yes. Immediately after the burnt offering, I was able to complete a very profitable trade.

burhczydx_5a_4.m: Just look at this heavy bag of gold!
r: I am very impressed. What was the trade?

burhczydx_5a_5.m: It was a very simple thing. Fast and easy gold.
r: Tell me, what was the trade for?

burhczydx_5a_6.m: I sold my cart! Together with the horse - now I even save the money for its food.
r: Ah. OK, but what do you intend to use to transport the next load?

burhczydx_5a_7.m: Oh, right. I hadn't thought of that. My father doesn't have another cart, so I will look for something else to do.
r: So we have to think about what else you might do. Do you have any musical talent?

burhczydx_5a_8.m: Oh yeah! I always liked to play the lute and sing! With the money I have I can buy the best lute in the country!
r: I wish you the best of luck!

burhczydx_5e.m: Before I leave, we should drink to a good start.

burhczydx_6a.m: ... THERE WAAAS A GIIIRL AT THE GAAAATE ...

r: Finally. Bravo! More! But not now, please.

burhczydx_6a_4.m: Hey, my biggest fan. How did you find me?

burhczydx_6a_5.m: Thank you, I know. What is your name again?

burhczydx_6a_5b.m: Eh, wait. Do you have any idea why the landlord is coming for me with a thick wooden club?
r: It's probably best that you promise him that you will not sing anymore.
You could sing in a troll band.

burhczydx_6a_7.m: Sigh. My mother always loved my music.
r: Your lute skills are actually quite good. Maybe just try it without singing.

burhczydx_6a_8.m: OK, I will try that. But I think it would be better if it were not here. The landlord is still looking at me suspiciously.

burhczydx_6e.m: The landlord is still watching me - I had better not move.

burhczydx_7a.m: Hey, nice to meet you again!
r: You forgot my name again, didn't you? I am $playername.

burhczydx_7a_3.m: Look here, my lute. The best instrument in the country. And I'm not allowed to play here.

burhczydx_7a_4.m: I played so well and charmingly, that the guests forgot everything around them.

burhczydx_7a_5.m: They even forgot to order something to drink.
r: And the landlord was not amused?

burhczydx_7a_6.m: Yes. Sigh. He forbade me to continue making music.

burhczydx_7a_7.m: Now I have to think again about what to do next.
r: I am sure you will come up with something.

burhczydx_7e.m: As soon as I know what I'm going to do next, I'll leave.

r: Hi Burhczyd. You remembered my name!

burhczydx_8a_2.m: Sure I did. And I also have learned a new profession. I am already rather good.
r: Great to hear! Tell me more.

burhczydx_8a_3.m: I talk to people in places like this. Taverns and such.

burhczydx_8a_4.m: We talk about everything; the world, magic rings, dragons, everything. We become more and more familiar.
r: And by doing that you get a beer or two?

burhczydx_8a_5.m: Ha ha ha. Much better. People start to trust me. A great feeling.

burhczydx_8a_6.m: And when they leave, they don't even miss their purse or jewels.

burhczydx_8a_7.m: Hush, not so loud. No, I'm not an ordinary pickpocket. I became a master thief.
r: Oh dear. I didn't expect that from you.

burhczydx_8a_8.m: I am finished here for now. As soon as the moment is right, I will disappear.

burhczydx_8e.m: As soon as the moment is right, I will go.

r: Why? Did you do something wrong?

burhczydx_9a_3.m: Yes, I did something very wrong.

burhczydx_9a_4.m: I never should have done that to a friend.

burhczydx_9a_5.m: I 'borrowed' some things from you the last time we met.

burhczydx_9a_6_81a.m: First of all, you can have back your 100 pieces of gold.

burhczydx_9a_6_82a.m: Here is your Necklace of the Undead. I didn't even wear it once.

burhczydx_9a_6_83a.m: This is your father's ring, I think.

burhczydx_9a_6_84a.m: Then we have a ruby gem - not of much worth, really.

burhczydx_9a_6_85a.m: Last but not least I proudly present: The Dagger of the Shadow Priests!

burhczydx_9a_6a.m: Oh, it was just a few trifles, nothing important. Here you go, have them all back again.

r: I did not expect that from you. But OK, you did a good job as master thief.

burhczydx_9a_8.m: That's what I wanted to hear.
r: And you are naughty in addition to that.
I don't suppose you are a member of the Thieves' Guild? I never heard of you.

burhczydx_9a_8a.m: You talk of Umar and his little gang? Are you also no one and nobody has seen you?

burhczydx_9a_8b.m: Don't look so irritated. Of course I know such internals. But no, I am no member of the guild. I prefer to be independent.

burhczydx_9a_8c.m: Honestly, I don't even know if this job is the right thing for me.
r: By the way - did you meet my brother Andor on your journeys?

burhczydx_9a_8d.m: Sure. I even trailed him for some time, because he had exhibited some interesting behaviour.
r: Interesting? Or perhaps strange? What did he do?

burhczydx_9a_8e.m: No no no, I won't tell you of course.

burhczydx_9a_8f.m: But here, take this little thing that I 'borrowed' from him.
r: A stuffed rat? Urgh. I will give it back to him as soon as possible.

burhczydx_9a_8g.m: Well, it's time to say goodbye. Farewell now.

burhczydx_9e.m: Before I leave, I have some business to do here.

Thieves02.2: After completing my first task I'm considered a member of Thieves' Guild. Now I have to perform a very risky task. Umar sent me to kidnap a noble woman from Feygard, without being discovered.
Thieves02.4: She was recently seen in the Foaming Flask tavern.
Thieves02.6: Umar gave me some advice. My strength is not always the solution. I must "use my tongue" to avoid raising suspicion in the tavern.
Thieves02.10: Ambelie Laumwill doesn't want to come with me peacefully. I cannot make a scene, or the guards will alert other patrols. Maybe talking with them would solve the situation.
Thieves02.15: I have "used my tongue" with the main Feygard soldier in the Foaming Flask tavern. He gave me permission to "escort back" Ambelie.
Thieves02.20: I knocked out Ambelie. I will take her back to the Guild.
Thieves02.21: I have decided not to kidnap Ambelie. I must think of another solution.
Thieves02.24: Ambelie gave me a very valuable necklace. I must talk with Umar and persuade him to no longer pursue her.
Thieves02.30: I safely brought Ambelie to the basement. However, keeping her here could be dangerous.
Thieves02.35: Umar believes there is a secure room for these types of "visitors". I should talk to Troublemaker.
Thieves02.40: I have talked to Troublemaker about the place Umar believes it's okay to safely keep the hostage.
Thieves02.45: Troublemaker has given me the key to the Guild brig. I should take Ambelie there and leave her to wake up.
Thieves02.50: I've inserted the key and moved the lever. A hatchway has opened in the room.
Thieves02.55: I left Ambelie in that ugly, dark, and cold place. I should go back.
Thieves02.60: Troublemaker gave me some bread for Ambelie. The guild doesn't want her to starve to death. Indeed, they want her to be as comfortable as possible. I must go to the brig again.
Thieves02.65: I gave the bread to Ambelie. I should report Troublemaker that I completed the job.
Thieves02.70: The job finally seems to be finished. I just have to talk with Umar again. However, I do not feel good about this. Kidnappings are definitely not my kind of job.
Thieves02.75: I completed this task successfully. Umar told me they have sent couriers to Feygard, and the ransom is almost guaranteed. He paid me for my work.
Thieves02.76: Umar took the necklace as compensation for my errors. Everything is fine again.

quest_burhczyd.10: You met Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye, a likable young man, in a tavern. He wanted to see the world and followed your advice to travel as a trader from city to city.
quest_burhczyd.20: In another tavern you met Burhczyd again. He never got any customers, because he had named his company 'Burhczyd afgz Dtaloumiye - Transports'. You told him to find an easier name.
quest_burhczyd.30: You saw Burhczyd in a tavern, but he still did not have any customers. You told him that 'B.A.D. Transports' was not a good idea either.
quest_burhczyd.40: Another place, another tavern, Burhczyd again sitting there. He did get a shipment from Remgard of almost fresh fish, but nobody wanted to buy it. You bought the entire cargo and got it disposed of.
quest_burhczyd.50: What a surprise - you met Burhczyd again in a tavern. He told you that he finally sold something successfully - his cart. The fool, how will he earn money now?
quest_burhczyd.60: In a tavern a bard sang in a high, shrill voice. It's an old acquaintance - Burhczyd. His singing was incredibly bad. Maybe he should just play his instrument without singing?
quest_burhczyd.70: You found Burhczyd collapsed at a table in the tavern, his lute lying in front of him. The landlord forbade him to play his lovely music, because then all the guests forgot to drink.
quest_burhczyd.80: Again you met Burhczyd in a tavern. He told you that he had become a master thief.
quest_burhczyd.90: When you met Burhczyd again, he gave you some of your things back.
quest_burhczyd.100: You've talked with a Knight of Elythom who happened to be an old acquaintance - Burhczyd. He had to hide from the Elythom, because he had 'borrowed' something of value from their leader.
quest_burhczyd.110: Burhczyd was no longer dressed like a knight of the Elythom. He said he's going to marry the prettiest girl in the world - she just doesn't know yet...
quest_burhczyd.120: You've met a very depressed Burhczyd. His love was going to marry a baker! Therefore, he bought an oven to outdo his rival.
quest_burhczyd.130: Burhczyd planned to bake larger and more beautiful loaves of bread in the tavern than the baker whom his love is going to marry. Yet he still had to learn how to bake.
quest_burhczyd.140:
Burhczyd has begun the life of a monk. Fasting was not at all easy for him.

[Quest is not completable at this time.]

sk.fightstyleUnarmedUnarmored: Fighting style: Way of the monk
